findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, cadence and read 3); plan (blocks O3, O6, O7); 11 11.2
findings.defect: The note makes a later read due at each sitting of blocks O3, O6 and O7, but no plan row carries it, and its merge try at a release sitting is not ordered against the candidate, the pre-tag check and the v1.0.0 tag.
findings.scenario: The maintainer runs O6 and O7 from the plan's rows, which say nothing of the read, so the read is skipped and the narrowing goes unread through the release; or the maintainer remembers it and runs read 3 at O7, merging a throwaway pull request whose revert, after decision 1, is itself a pull request waiting on the four required checks. 11 11.2 counts a result on the candidate when, from the candidate's commit to the v1.0.0 tag, only docs/ and root Markdown paths differ, and tools/ci acceptance checks that before the tag, so a merge reverted before the tag changes no path and an unreverted non-docs payload is caught by the pre-tag check rather than shipped; hence Advisory, not Required: the text does not make O7 tag the wrong commit, it costs a stalled sitting or a new candidate when the payload is not empty.
findings.change: Each of O3, O6 and O7 names the later read in 'What the maintainer does' and its time in the wait column; the note says the read runs before the candidate tag at O6 and after the v1.0.0 tag at O7 (or skips the merge try once a candidate exists), and that its payloads are empty commits. Cost: three plan cells and one sentence in the note.
findings.evidence: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:122-124 'one for each later read, which is due at each sitting of blocks O3, O6 and O7 of the plan'; docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:87 'try four things with throwaway payloads'; :97 'the merge reverted'; grep -n 'later read|entry of the note|token narrowing|narrowed' docs/plan.md hits only lines 221 and 319; docs/spec/11-host-probes.md:124-126 'the only paths that differ are under `docs/` or are Markdown files at the repository root'; :130 '`tools/ci acceptance` checks that for each block B result'.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, read 2 and the verdict); plan (block O8, Recommendation); ADR 0011 decision 2
findings.defect: Read 2 expects 'the setting names one socket; that socket holds the signing key', and the verdict requires read 2 to match, so a narrowing that stops the forwarding by forwarding nothing reads not narrowed, although ADR 0011 decision 2 decides only that the authentication key's forwarding stops and R16-11 states that how is the maintainer's choice.
findings.scenario: The maintainer, following ADR 0011 rather than O8's recommendation, stops forwarding any agent socket; read 2 finds no socket, the entry reads not narrowed, the four rows never fire and item h never runs. Advisory because O8's recommendation leads a maintainer who follows the plan to a signing-only socket, which matches; the defect bites only off the recommended path. Also, part 3 compares only the signing key's fingerprint with the account page, while part 2's 'no GitHub authentication key' needs every forwarded fingerprint checked against the authentication list.
findings.change: Read 2's expected answer becomes 'no forwarded socket holds a key the account page lists under authentication keys; when a socket is forwarded, the signing key is listed only under signing keys', with each forwarded fingerprint compared. No ADR change is needed. Cost: two sentences in the note.
findings.evidence: docs/notes/maintainer-block-of-ci-bootstrap.md:158-161 'Expected: the setting names one socket; that socket holds the signing key and no GitHub authentication key; and the signing key's fingerprint is listed on the page only under signing keys'; :179 'The token is narrowed when the A16 read and the three parts of read 2 match what is expected'; docs/adr/0011-bind-the-administrator-to-the-required-checks-and-narrow-the-sandbox-s-github-token.md:93-94 'The forwarding of the GitHub authentication SSH key to the sandbox stops too'; docs/reviews/round-16.md R16-11 write pass 'how the forwarding stops is the maintainer's choice'.

findings.section: the note on the maintainer block (The token narrowing, the entry rule); index (Deferred decisions opening; rows 279, 283, 351, 353)
findings.defect: The note makes a later not narrowed entry 'an event of those four rows too', but the four trigger cells name only the first narrowed entry, the index says a row leaves the table when its event happens and the decision is made, and a re-narrowing after a not narrowed entry is no event at all.
findings.scenario: The first narrowed entry fires the four rows, each is decided and leaves the table; a later read finds an extra permission and writes not narrowed; the note says the decisions are reviewed again, but the rows are gone, their cells never named this event, and nobody files the `deferred` issue the index requires for a review-only event; when the token is narrowed again, nothing reopens what was decided on the not narrowed premise.
findings.change: Each of the four trigger cells adds 'or a later entry whose verdict differs from the one before it', the note says a row that left the table is restored with its last decision when such an entry is written, and O8's pass (or the note) says the maintainer files one `deferred` issue per row the entry fires. Cost: four cell edits and two sentences.

A cell states what holds and the event'; docs/spec.md:279 'or the token is narrowed, as the first narrowed entry of [the note on the maintainer block] records it'.

findings.defect: The opening ties the maintainer-pushes-tags working agreement to the operator's token being held 'until block O8', which reads as if the reason lapses after O8, although whether the narrowed token passes the tag ruleset's bypass is not measured, and never is when O8 runs after release.yml.
findings.scenario: After O8 an agent session reads the opening, concludes the tag ruleset now binds the sandbox's token, and treats the working agreement as moot; nothing measured supports that, and the index row says the tag answer can stay not measured.
findings.change: 'which the sandbox holds until block O8, and whose narrowed successor's reach on `v*` tags the entry of the note measures, or records as not measured'. Cost: one clause.
findings.evidence: docs/plan.md:202-204 'the two `v*` tags, which the maintainer pushes by working agreement, since the tag ruleset does not bind the operator's token, which the sandbox holds until block O8'; docs/spec.md:348 'whether it can create a `v*` tag through the tag ruleset's bypass is measured only by an entry made before `release.yml` lands, and stays not measured otherwise'.

what_is_missing: The later-read cadence in the O3, O6 and O7 rows, with its order inside a release sitting and an empty-payload rule; a named pull request for decision 1's answer and S2 in O8's Unblocks; a read 2 expected answer that matches ADR 0011 decision 2 and checks every forwarded fingerprint; the not-narrowed and re-narrowed events in the four trigger cells and a rule for rows that already left the table; who files the `deferred` issues for the review-only token events; item h gated on the newest entry and a date on the fourth part; the narrowed-state text of the 05 5.4 token row and row 348 and the step that writes it.
postmortem: The maintainer works from the plan's block rows, and the pass put three obligations elsewhere: later reads (note only), the `deferred` issues for the token events (nowhere), and the pull request for decision 1's answer (unnamed). The reads lapse, or run mid-O7 and stall the tag behind a revert pull request. A maintainer who stops the forwarding by forwarding nothing, as ADR 0011 allows, gets not narrowed, so the signed approval record and the ruleset reread never reopen before v1.0.0 and 05 5.4's 'process only against an agent' stays the only control. The tag working agreement is read as moot after O8 on the strength of 'until block O8', which nothing measured. The rows a regression entry 'returns' never had a narrowed state, and the rows it 'reopens' had left the table. Unsaid: every control here is [review] and read by the person who sits, and no success criterion fails while the token stays broad except through S2's fallback. Crosses the note (The token narrowing), 10 10.2 a, g, h, plan opening and O3, O6, O7, O8, the index's Deferred decisions opening and rows 279, 283, 348, 351, 353, 05 5.4, ADR 0011 decisions 1 and 2, 11 11.2, S1 and S2.
lens_critique: Reading success only through S1 to S11 under-weights process controls no S row measures: the token narrowing and the bypass removal touch success only through S2's fallback wording, so this lens can call them complete when they are only scheduled, and it tends to grade their seams Advisory because no criterion turns red. It also reads text, not calendars: whether an obligation lands on a sitting the maintainer actually holds is outside the S rows.
missing_viewpoint: The operator as the one human in the loop, whose sittings and attention are the budget every maintainer block and [review] control spends; L14 is the maintainer on duty for incidents, not the person whose calendar the blocks consume and whose missed step silently disables a control.
out_of_scope: The salvage text of the round-16 pass (RJ-338, 01 1.6, 03 3.8, 08 8.5, I17), reviewed by other lenses; the date discrepancy of the first four tries (2026-10-07 versus 2026-10-08); plan O1 describing items a to d as still to run.
